questions.text: What problem is solved by Dijikstra banker' algorithm?
questions.solution:
The banker's algorithm checks, before granting a request, that the system stays in a safe state. That is deadlock avoidance.

Answer: Deadlock avoidance

questions.text:
Consider the set of processes with arrival time (in milliseconds). CPU burst time (in milliseconds), and priority (0 is the highest priority) shown below. None of the processes have I/O burst time.

The average waiting time (in milliseconds) of all the processes using preemptive priority scheduling algorithm is __________
questions.solution:
Preemptive priority (0 = highest):
P1 0-2, P4 2-5, P2 5-33, P4 33-40, P1 40-49, P3 49-51, P5 51-67

Waiting: P1 49 [latex]-[/latex] 11 = 38, P2 0, P3 51 [latex]-[/latex] 12 [latex]-[/latex] 2 = 37, P4 40 [latex]-[/latex] 2 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 28, P5 67 [latex]-[/latex] 9 [latex]-[/latex] 16 = 42
Average = 145 / 5 = 29

Answer: 29

questions.text:
A system shares 9 tape drives. The current allocation and maximum requirement of tape drives for three processes are shown below:

Which of the following best describes current state of the system ?
questions.solution:
Allocated = 3 + 1 + 3 = 7, so 2 drives are free. Remaining needs: P1 4, P2 5, P3 2.
P3 can finish (needs 2) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] free 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P1 can finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] free 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P2 can finish. A safe sequence exists, and no process is stuck right now.

Answer: Safe, Not Deadlocked

questions.text:
In a file allocation system, which of the following allocation schemes(s) can be used if no external fragmentation is allowed?
I. Contiguous
II. Linked
III. Indexed
questions.solution:
Contiguous allocation needs one big continuous hole, which causes external fragmentation. Linked and indexed allocation can use any free block anywhere, so they have no external fragmentation.

Answer: II and III only
